title: AWS CWI Training in Memphis, TN: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Memphis welders in bridges, rail, data centers and plants: corporate on site, online at your pace, or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Memphis, Tennessee: Six Days for Bridge, Rail, Logistics and Plant Welding Inspectors
html:
In May 2021 a routine inspection found a fractured tie girder on the Hernando de Soto Bridge, the I-40 crossing of the Mississippi at Memphis, and the bridge closed for roughly three months. Investigators later traced the crack to weld repairs made when the girder was fabricated decades earlier. Few local events make the case for welding inspection more plainly. Memphis welds the steel of a freight city: bridges, rail equipment, warehouses, data centers, a refinery, a steel mill and power plants. Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination in a six-day (6-day) course covering Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. It is offered three ways: corporate delivery at an employer's facility, online study at your own pace, or six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification; Atlantis is a preparation provider and certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in Memphis, and the company's two offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. For a quote, send a Memphis CWI enquiry.

Three formats for Memphis candidates

The same six-day outline sits under every format. The first two days build Part A knowledge: welding and cutting processes, AWS terminology, joint design, welding symbols, metallurgy, destructive and nondestructive testing, discontinuities, safety and the inspector's ethics. Day three prepares for the practical, day four is spent inside your chosen code book, day five is timed practice papers, and day six revisits weak spots and covers exam logistics. The detailed plan is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

  1. Corporate, for an employer preparing a group. A bridge fabricator, railcar shop, plant contractor or structural steel company can have the six days delivered at its own facility, with practical work on its own gauges and welds and code work in the book its people build to.
  2. Online, for an individual. You get a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, plus an instructor who answers questions as you work. There are no scheduled class times, which suits anyone on nights at a hub or a distribution center.
  3. One-to-one, for a single candidate who wants the instructor's full attention: six days of one-to-one sessions, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

All practice questions are Atlantis originals, written to the subject areas AWS publishes. None is taken from an AWS examination, and AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

What the I-40 bridge fracture teaches a CWI candidate

The forensic findings, as reported by ENR, read like a list of CWI exam topics. Two weld repairs made during fabrication at thickness transitions in the tie girder were much wider than the other transition welds and laid down in a different sequence. Investigators linked the hydrogen cracking that followed to restraint, improper preheat and/or contaminated welding electrodes, and noted that the repairs were made without a fracture control plan. The cracks were not caught during fabrication or by an ultrasonic test in 1982, and the eventual fracture was visible in inspection images from 2016 that went unreported.

Each of those points maps onto something the examination covers. Preheat, hydrogen and restraint cracking are Part A metallurgy. Spotting a repair that does not match the approved procedure is the kind of judgment Part B tests when you check work against the documents you are handed. And AWS D1.5, the bridge welding code that AWS offers as a Part C book, contains a fracture control plan for nonredundant members, which is exactly the category of member that failed here. The reports also pointed to a culture in which inspection staff did not feel able to question what they found. A CWI's duty to report what is actually there, even when it is unwelcome, is part of the ethics material on the exam for good reason.

The Memphis welding economy

Freight by air, rail, river and road

FedEx runs its world hub at Memphis International Airport. Five Class I railroads, BNSF, CN, CSX, Norfolk Southern and Union Pacific, serve the area, and I-40 and I-55 cross the city beside the Mississippi River port. Freight on that scale needs a constant supply of maintenance welding: hangar and terminal structures, airport and yard equipment, intermodal cranes, railcar and locomotive repair, barge terminals and fleeting areas, and the truck and trailer shops along the interstates.

Data centers and the power behind them

xAI built its first Colossus AI training cluster in Memphis by repurposing a shuttered Electrolux factory, and in 2025 bought a warehouse of about one million square feet in the city for a second cluster. It also acquired a former power plant site in Southaven, just across the Mississippi state line, and has relied on gas turbines for on-site power. Projects of that kind combine structural steel, cooling-water and fuel gas piping and generating equipment, so they draw D1.1 structural inspectors alongside piping inspectors working to ASME rules.

Refining, steel and power

Valero operates a refinery on the south side of Memphis, Nucor runs a steel mill in the city, and the Tennessee Valley Authority and the local utility operate generating plants and substations. Refinery piping is built and repaired to ASME B31.3 and power piping to B31.1, both with procedures and welders qualified under Section IX. Mill maintenance keeps repair welders working on heavy equipment through the year.

Warehouses and distribution buildings

The distribution economy also builds. Large warehouses and cross-dock buildings, with steel frames, roof structures, mezzanines and equipment supports, are a steady source of structural welding to AWS D1.1 and of special inspection under the building code.

Who hires CWIs in and around Memphis

  • Bridge fabricators and highway contractors. Work for the Tennessee, Arkansas and Mississippi transportation departments brings D1.5 shop and field inspection.
  • Railcar and locomotive repair shops. Repairs and modifications for the railroads and car owners need inspectors who understand workmanship and qualification on rolling stock.
  • Industrial and data center contractors. Structural, piping and equipment installation on large projects needs QC staff on both the structural and piping sides.
  • Refinery and power plant contractors. Maintenance and outage work at the Valero refinery and at TVA and utility plants calls for inspectors fluent in Section IX and the B31 piping codes.
  • Structural steel fabricators and erectors. Warehouse, hospital and commercial building programs across the metro need D1.1 inspection in the shop and on site.
  • Third-party inspection firms and owner's representatives. Vendor surveillance and field inspection across three states is a common route for independent CWIs.

Choosing your Part C book in Memphis

AWS lets you choose the code for the open-book Part C from its list: AWS D1.1 (structural steel), API 1104 (pipelines), D1.2 (aluminum), D1.5 (bridges), D15.1 (railcars and locomotives), D17.1 (aerospace fusion welding), an ASME option of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. The Memphis economy points candidates at five of them.

If you mostly inspectChooseWhy it fits Memphis work
Steel bridge girders, repairs and retrofitsAWS D1.5River and highway bridges, with the fracture control plan for nonredundant members
Railcars and locomotivesAWS D15.1Written for rolling stock repair and manufacture
Warehouses, data center steel, equipment supportsAWS D1.1The structural code behind most building and industrial steel
Refinery, power plant and process pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Procedure and welder qualification plus piping examination and acceptance
Pipelines feeding plants and terminalsAPI 1104The pipeline welding standard federal safety rules incorporate

Study the edition AWS names for the exam, which may lag the newest printing. Background reading: AWS D1.5, AWS D1.1 and API 1104.

The AWS West Tennessee Section

AWS has a West Tennessee Section, Section 106, named for this end of the state. Its own website is candid that the section has been inactive for several years; a group of members is restarting it with quarterly meetings, and a section meeting and officer election was announced for November 2026. For a Memphis candidate that is an opportunity as much as a gap. A restarting section needs volunteers, and its meetings are a good place to meet the inspectors and QC managers who can verify your experience for AWS. Members living on the Mississippi or Arkansas side of the metro can also look up the sections serving those states through aws.org.

Where Memphis welders train

Several institutions feed the local welding workforce. Southwest Tennessee Community College reopened its welding program as part of a multi-million-dollar Department of Labor workforce grant aimed at the Memphis skills gap; one early class of fourteen students earned 105 AWS welding certifications between them, welder tests rather than inspector credentials. The Tennessee College of Applied Technology at Memphis, William R. Moore College of Technology and Arkansas State University Mid-South in West Memphis took part in the same regional grant, administered by the Greater Memphis Alliance for a Competitive Workforce. Plenty of Memphis welders also learned on the job in fabrication shops, rail yards and plant maintenance crews.

That training can matter for eligibility. AWS lists four years of welding-related experience for candidates who completed trade or vocational courses, compared with five for a high school diploma, though AWS decides which courses count. Keep your certificates, transcripts and welder test records; they also help document the work history AWS asks you to verify.

Booking the exam from Memphis

The Memphis metro spans Tennessee, Mississippi and Arkansas, but the CWI is a national AWS credential, so your state of residence makes no difference to eligibility. When AWS accepts your application, it sends a confirmation with an eligibility code, and you use that code to book the computer-based Fundamentals and Code Application parts with Prometric; AWS says Prometric has well over 100 centers in the United States. The practical is a separate booking. AWS runs Part B only at its own seminar and examination locations on dates it sets, so Memphis candidates should check the AWS schedule early and expect that travel may be needed.

The exam has three parts. Part A asks 150 questions on fundamentals. Part B combines practical tasks using equipment AWS provides with 46 questions. Part C gives you about 50 to 65 questions with your code book open. AWS requires at least 72 percent on each part. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org; the Atlantis course is quoted separately on request, and the CWI exam budget planner lists the other costs to plan for. For how candidates tend to do on each part, see CWI results by part.

Studying around freight peaks and project deadlines

Memphis work has its own calendar. Parcel and distribution operations peak before the year-end holidays, data center and warehouse schedules tighten as handover approaches, and plant outages tend to come in spring and fall. The online format lets you work in the gaps. One approach: cover the fundamentals when overtime eases, keep a tabbed code book with you and look up the clauses that govern the welds you inspect, practise Part B measurements with fillet, undercut and bridge cam gauges on scrap and test coupons, and keep the timed papers for the last weeks before your Prometric date. Write questions down as they come and send them to the instructor.

Corporate: six days at a Memphis-area employer

A company preparing several people can have the six days delivered at its own facility. A bridge fabricator can work the practical day on its own girder welds and spend the code day in D1.5; a railcar shop can use D15.1; a contractor serving data center and plant projects can split the code day between D1.1 and the ASME book. Dates can be planned around peak season, outages and project milestones. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually and must meet the experience and vision requirements personally; an employer cannot apply on someone's behalf.

One-to-one: online or in person

Six days of one-to-one sessions give one candidate the instructor's undivided time, either online or in person at a location agreed when booking. The outline is the same, but the hours follow your needs: fabrication math and symbol reading for a strong practical welder, code navigation for someone who has never used a code book, or measurement and document drills for someone returning to Part B. Companies sometimes choose it for a single new QC hire who must be ready before a project starts.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS sets the years of welding-related experience by education level. With a high school diploma or equivalent it is five years; with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, one; associate degrees, technical coursework and trade courses fall in between, and less schooling raises the requirement. The work has to be verifiable and tied to welded products. AWS also requires a Visual Acuity Record on its form, showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more with or without correction and a color perception test, done by a qualified practitioner and dated within the period AWS allows before the exam. The complete table is on the CWI course page, and the CWI requirements and career guide covers the details. Candidates without enough years can consider the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI), who inspects under a CWI or Senior CWI.

After the CWI: career paths in Memphis

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewal filings at the third and sixth years and recertification at the ninth. In Memphis the next step often follows the sector. Bridge inspectors deepen their D1.5 knowledge; note that safety inspection of in-service highway bridges is a separate discipline with its own federal training requirements. Rail inspectors build D15.1 experience. Plant inspectors move toward owner's inspection and quality management. Many add nondestructive testing so they can carry out magnetic particle, penetrant or ultrasonic tests themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its NDT technicians after training and documented experience, and Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A-based training: see NDT training in Memphis, VT Level 1 training, magnetic particle testing in Memphis and weld inspection services. Those who come to run inspection programs can aim for the AWS Senior CWI; see the Senior CWI pathway. For a side-by-side of credentials, read CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II.

Nearby CWI pages and a Memphis quote

Other CWI exam prep pages in the region: Nashville, St. Louis, Birmingham and New Orleans. To rehearse inspection steps in a browser, see Practical NDT for Memphis and the welding workshop simulator.

To get a quote, tell us which format you prefer (corporate, online or one-to-one), how many people want to prepare, each person's education and welding experience in outline, and the Part C book each expects to choose. For delivery at your site, include the location, the gauges and sample welds available, and any peak season, outage or project dates to work around. Use the Memphis CWI enquiry form.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis CWI classroom in Memphis?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Memphis. The six-day course is available as corporate delivery at your employer's facility, as online study at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, or as six days of one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking. See the outline.

AWS. The American Welding Society administers the examination, reviews eligibility and issues the certification. The Atlantis course prepares candidates and certifies nobody; it is not approved or endorsed by AWS.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits bridge work in the Memphis area?
faq.a: AWS D1.5, the bridge welding code. It covers bridge-specific qualification and acceptance and includes the fracture control plan for nonredundant members. See AWS D1.5.

faq.q: I inspect railcar repairs at a Memphis yard. Is there a Part C book for that?
faq.a: Yes. AWS D15.1, the railroad welding specification for cars and locomotives, is one of the Part C options AWS offers.

faq.q: Where do Memphis candidates sit the exam?
faq.a: Fundamentals and Code Application are computer-based; you reserve them with Prometric once AWS sends your eligibility code. The practical runs only at AWS seminar and examination locations on dates AWS chooses, so a Memphis candidate may have to travel for it.

faq.q: I live in DeSoto County, Mississippi, or West Memphis, Arkansas. Does that change anything?
faq.a: No. The CWI is a national AWS certification, so the state you live in does not affect eligibility or how you book the exam.

faq.q: Can a data center or plant contractor have the six days delivered on site?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings the six days to your facility, uses your gauges and welds, and can split the code day between D1.1 and the ASME book. Request a quote.

faq.q: Should I choose one-to-one sessions online or in person?
faq.a: Either works. Online sessions suit shift workers and anyone outside the city; in person, at a location agreed when booking, suits candidates who want to practise measurement with physical gauges and samples alongside the instructor.

faq.q: Are the practice questions real AWS exam questions?
faq.a: No. Every practice question and timed paper is written by Atlantis to the subject areas AWS publishes. Atlantis has no access to the live examination.

faq.q: Is there an active AWS section in Memphis?
faq.a: AWS has a West Tennessee Section (Section 106). Its website says it has been inactive for several years and that members are restarting it with quarterly meetings, with a meeting and officer election announced for November 2026.
